title_en: Germany Eurasia Exchange Co., Ltd. v. Suifenhe Qingyun Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. — dispute over cooperation agreement
ruling_gist_en: Where the parties to a foreign-related contract expressly agree in the contract to be subject to the jurisdiction of the court at the place of contract conclusion, and subsequently enter into a supplementary agreement in another place regarding matters not covered by the contract, but the supplementary agreement does not amend the original jurisdictional clause, the validity of the jurisdictional clause in the contract is not affected by the execution of the supplementary agreement, and the contract dispute between the parties shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the court at the place where the contract was concluded.

full_text_en:
German Asia-Europe Exchange Co., Ltd. v. Suifenhe Qingyun Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. — dispute over cooperation agreement

Ruling Summary

Where the parties to an涉外 contract have explicitly agreed in the contract to be subject to the jurisdiction of the court at the place where the contract was signed, and subsequently enter into a supplementary agreement in another place regarding matters not covered by the contract, but the supplementary agreement does not modify the original jurisdiction clause, the validity of the jurisdiction clause in the contract is not altered by the execution of the supplementary agreement, and any contractual dispute arising between the parties shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the court at the place where the contract was signed.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2006) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 8

Appellant (original defendant): German Asia-Europe Exchange Co., Ltd. (AEEXchange Gesellschaft für Wirtschaft Ausbildung Wissenschaft und Kultur mbH/AEEXchange GmbH). Address: Poststr. 24, D-53111 Bonn, Germany.

Legal representative: Xia Tian, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Qihuai, attorney at Beijing Lanpeng Law Firm.

Appellee (original plaintiff): Suifenhe Qingyun Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. Address: No. 88 Changjiang Road, Suifenhe City, Heilongjiang Province, the People's Republic of China.

Legal representative: Qin Yuliang, Chairman of the company.

The appellant, German Asia-Europe Exchange Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as German Asia-Europe Company), appealed against the civil ruling (2005) Hei Gao Shang Wai Chu Zi No. 1 rendered by the High People's Court of Heilongjiang Province (hereinafter referred to as the original trial court) in the case of a dispute over a cooperation agreement with the appellee, Suifenhe Qingyun Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qingyun Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Wang Chong as presiding judge, acting judges Chen Jizhong and Zhou Xiang participating in the deliberations, and Liang Ying as the clerk. The case is now concluded.

On October 27, 2005, Qingyun Company filed a lawsuit with the original trial court, requesting the rescission of the "Cooperation Agreement on 'Section D of the Cologne Chinese Commodity Wholesale Market in Germany'" entered into between Qingyun Company and German Asia-Europe Company, and requesting an order that German Asia-Europe Company return the entrance fee of RMB 22,400,735.37 and compensate for project operating expenses of RMB 220,482.94. Qingyun Company alleged: On June 30, 2004, Qingyun Company and German Asia-Europe Company signed a "Cooperation Agreement on 'Section D of the Cologne Chinese Commodity Wholesale Market in Germany'" in Qingdao City, Shandong Province, China, agreeing to cooperate on the project of soliciting investment for Section D of the Cologne Chinese Commodity Wholesale Market in Germany. Article 8, paragraph 4 of the agreement stipulated: "If any dispute arises between Party A and Party B regarding this agreement or the project involved herein, the parties shall resolve it through negotiation; if negotiation fails, the dispute shall be subject to the jurisdiction or arbitration of the court at the place where the agreement was signed." Paragraph 5 stipulated: "The law applicable to disputes arising from this agreement between Party A and Party B shall be the law of the People's Republic of China." On January 26, 2005, Qingyun Company and German Asia-Europe Company signed a "Supplementary Agreement to the 'Cooperation Agreement on Section D of the Cologne Chinese Commodity Wholesale Market in Germany'" in Suifenhe City, Heilongjiang Province, China, concerning matters such as business investigation visas and entrance fees related to the cooperation project.

German Asia-Europe Company raised an objection to jurisdiction, arguing that this case is an foreign-related case, and the place of performance of the disputed agreement, the domicile of the defendant, the location of the immovable property involved in the dispute, and the place of jurisdiction agreed upon in the agreement are all not in Heilongjiang Province. According to Article 243 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the original trial court has no jurisdiction over this case. It requested that the case be transferred to a court with jurisdiction or that the lawsuit be dismissed.

The original trial court held upon review: According to Article 244 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, "Parties to a dispute over an foreign-related contract or foreign-related property rights and interests may, by written agreement, choose the court of a place that has actual connection with the dispute to have jurisdiction." In the cooperation agreement involved in this case, the parties agreed: "If any dispute arises regarding this agreement or the project involved herein, ... the dispute shall be subject to the jurisdiction or arbitration of the court at the place where the agreement was signed." This agreement represents the true intention of the parties regarding contractual jurisdiction, does not violate the provisions of the laws of the People's Republic of China, and is lawful and valid. Therefore, disputes arising from the cooperation agreement shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the court at the place where the agreement was signed. After the parties signed the cooperation agreement in Qingdao City, Shandong Province, they later signed a supplementary agreement to the cooperation agreement in Suifenhe City, Heilongjiang Province. This supplementary agreement is an integral part of the cooperation agreement. Therefore, both Qingdao City and Suifenhe City are places where the cooperation agreement was signed. Consequently, the People's Court of Heilongjiang Province has jurisdiction over this dispute. The parties' agreement on jurisdiction does not violate the provisions on hierarchical jurisdiction, and therefore the original trial court's assumption of jurisdiction over this case is not improper. In summary, the objection to jurisdiction raised by the defendant, German Asia-Europe Company, lacks factual and legal basis. Pursuant to Article 38 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: The objection to jurisdiction raised by German Asia-Europe Company is rejected.

German Asia-Europe Company, dissatisfied with the original trial court's ruling, appealed to this Court, arguing: 1. The original trial court's ruling found unclear facts. The signing place of the cooperation agreement was Qingdao City, but the signing place of the supplementary agreement to the cooperation agreement was not in Suifenhe City. On November 3, 2004, the legal representatives of the parties signed Supplementary Agreement (I) in Shanghai City concerning issues such as the start and end dates of the cooperation agreement. The signing place of Supplementary Agreement (I) was Shanghai City. On January 24, 2005, the parties negotiated and reached an agreement on issues such as the entrance fee in Suifenhe City. Because Xia Tian did not bring the company seal, he returned to Beijing on January 26 and brought back Supplementary Agreement (II), which had been drafted and signed and sealed by Qingyun Company. He then signed and sealed it in Beijing and forwarded it to Qingyun Company. According to the relevant provisions of Chinese law, where the parties sign and seal the contract in different places, the place of the last signature or seal is the place where the contract is concluded. Therefore, the signing place of Supplementary Agreement (II) should be Beijing City. 2. The original trial court's ruling applied the law incorrectly. The original trial court cited Article 244 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, holding that this case should be subject to the jurisdiction of the court at the signing place of the supplementary agreement. A supplementary agreement is part of the principal contract, but it does not mean that the signing place of the supplementary agreement is equivalent to the signing place of the principal contract. When the parties signed the cooperation agreement, they agreed to be subject to the jurisdiction of the court at the place where the agreement was signed. Since no supplementary agreement had been signed at that time, the true intention of the parties referred to the court at the place where the principal contract was signed, not including the signing place of the supplementary agreement. Moreover, the signing place of the supplementary agreement is not in Heilongjiang Province. 3. Article 8, paragraph 4 of the cooperation agreement in this case stipulates that cooperative disputes shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the court at the signing place of the agreement, i.e., this case shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court, the place where the principal contract was signed. Even if the jurisdiction clause in the cooperation agreement was unclear, the original trial court still has no jurisdiction, and the original trial court's assumption of jurisdiction over this case does not meet the circumstances provided in Article 243 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. It requested: Dismiss Qingyun Company's lawsuit or transfer the case to a court with jurisdiction.

Qingyun Company did not provide a written defense.

This Court holds: The dispute in this case concerns an objection to jurisdiction, which is a procedural matter. The resolution of procedural issues in a case shall be governed by the law of the forum, i.e., the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Article 3 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China clearly provides: "Any civil litigation brought within the territory of the People's Republic of China concerning property relations and personal relations among citizens, legal persons, other organizations, and between them shall be governed by this Law."

Article 8, paragraph 4 of the "Cooperation Agreement on 'Section D of the Cologne Chinese Commodity Wholesale Market in Germany'" on which Qingyun Company bases its lawsuit stipulates: "If any dispute arises regarding this agreement or the project involved herein, ... the dispute shall be subject to the jurisdiction or arbitration of the court at the place where the agreement was signed." The parties have no dispute that this agreement was signed in Qingdao City, Shandong Province. Article 244 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Parties to a dispute over an foreign-related contract or foreign-related property rights and interests may, by written agreement, choose the court of a place that has actual connection with the dispute to have jurisdiction." Therefore, the parties' choice of the court at the place where the cooperation agreement was signed to have jurisdiction over this case in the cooperation agreement complies with the above legal provisions, and this jurisdiction clause shall be deemed valid. According to the agreement, the court at the place where the cooperation agreement was signed, i.e., the People's Court of Qingdao City, has jurisdiction over the cooperative dispute. The reason given by the original trial court for rejecting German Asia-Europe Company's objection to jurisdiction was that the supplementary agreement to the cooperation agreement was signed in Suifenhe City, Heilongjiang Province, and thus Suifenhe City was also a place where the cooperation agreement was signed, so the original trial court had jurisdiction over this case. The above reason is erroneous. This case is not a question of how to determine the place of signing when there are multiple signing locations for the "Cooperation Agreement on 'Section D of the Cologne Chinese Commodity Wholesale Market in Germany'" signed between the parties; rather, it is a question of whether the jurisdiction clause chosen by the parties is valid and whether the parties have changed the jurisdiction clause. When the parties signed the cooperation agreement, they explicitly chose the court at the place of signing of that agreement as the court to have jurisdiction over cooperative disputes. In fact, the parties had clearly chosen the People's Court of Qingdao City as the court of jurisdiction. Although the parties later supplemented the cooperation agreement in other locations, the supplementary agreement did not modify the jurisdiction clause in any way. Therefore, the jurisdiction clause in the cooperation agreement is binding on both parties to this case. Where the jurisdiction clause chosen in the cooperation agreement is valid, the original trial court's exercise of jurisdiction over the cooperative dispute based on the so-called signing place of the supplementary agreement lacks factual and legal basis. German Asia-Europe Company's appeal ground that the original trial court has no jurisdiction over this case is well-founded, and the original trial court's ruling should be reversed. According to Paragraph 2, Article 2 of the "Notice on Issues Concerning the Acceptance of First-Instance Civil and Economic Dispute Cases by Higher People's Courts" issued by this Court on April 9, 1999, the dispute amount for the Shandong High People's Court to accept first-instance foreign-related and Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan-related economic dispute cases shall not be less than RMB 30 million. The amount claimed by the original plaintiff Qingyun Company is approximately RMB 24 million. Therefore, this case shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province.

In conclusion, pursuant to Articles 38, 154, and 244 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

1. The civil ruling (2005) Hei Gao Shang Wai Chu Zi No. 1 of the High People's Court of Heilongjiang Province is set aside;

2. This case shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 50 and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 50 shall be borne by Qingyun Company.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Chong
Acting Judge: Chen Jizhong
Acting Judge: Zhou Xiang

April 20, 2006

Clerk: Liang Ying

[Introduction of the Presiding Judge]

Senior Judge Wang Chong: Born in 1955, Master of Laws, served as Deputy Chief Judge of the Fourth Civil Division of the Supreme People's Court from 2003.
